issue_title: Let users reset a forgotten password by email
issue_body:
Users who forget their password have to email support today.

Add `POST /password-resets` taking an `email`. When the email belongs to an account, send a reset link to it; the link expires after 30 minutes and works once. The response is `202` whether or not the email matched, so the endpoint does not reveal which emails have accounts. Repeated reset requests for the same email must be throttled so the endpoint cannot be used to flood someone's inbox.

plan.summary: Add POST /password-resets that emails a single-use reset link and throttles repeated requests per email.

approach.description: Add migration 0033 creating reset_tokens (token_hash, account_id, expires_at, used_at), with a down migration.
Add POST /password-resets: look up the account by email; when found, store a token expiring 30 minutes out and send the link; return 202 either way.
Add GET /password-resets/{token}, which refuses an expired or used token with 410 and otherwise lets the user set a new password.
Add internal/throttle/email.go, a per-email counter over a sliding 30-minute window allowing three sends; POST /password-resets consults it before sending.

verification.test_strategy: Handler tests with a fake clock and a fake mailer: a known and an unknown email both get 202 and only the known one sends; a link opened at 31 minutes is refused; a used link is refused; four requests send three links.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR and run the 0033 down migration; outstanding reset links stop working.

acceptance_criteria.statement: POST /password-resets for an email with an account returns HTTP 202 and sends one reset link to that email.
POST /password-resets for an email with no account returns HTTP 202 and sends nothing.
A reset link opened 31 minutes after it was sent returns HTTP 410 and leaves the password unchanged.
A reset link used once returns HTTP 410 when opened again.
A fourth POST /password-resets for the same email within 30 minutes still returns HTTP 202 but sends no reset link.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Inferred from the issue's throttling requirement: the window is the issue's 30-minute window, and three requests leave room for a user who mistypes twice.

risks_and_assumptions: The mailer is the existing transactional mail client.

catching_examples.note: ac-reset-throttle-fourth is not warranted as written: its 30 minutes is the link expiry, not a throttle window, and the issue gives no window or count.

ac-reset-throttle-fourth cites the issue's 30-minute window, but that clause is the reset link's lifetime. The count of three is precedent, not a requirement, and the plan cites no place the issue requires it.
The criterion on a fourth POST /password-resets within 30 minutes takes its window from the link expiry, a different clause; the issue asks for throttling but states no window.

ac-reset-throttle-fourth is inferred and blocking. It presents 30 minutes as the issue's window, but the only 30 minutes in the issue is how long a reset link stays valid; the issue asks that repeated requests be throttled and gives no count. Both the window and the count of three need a cited source, or the criterion should be non-blocking.
ac-reset-throttle-fourth introduces specific values the issue never states: in the issue 30 minutes is the link-expiry time, and the rationale cites no source for allowing three sends.
The issue states no throttle window and no send limit; the 30 minutes and the three sends in ac-reset-throttle-fourth are values the plan invented.

non_catching_examples.note: ac-reset-throttle-fourth needs a fake-clock test that sends four requests and counts the reset links the fake mailer received.
The per-email counter in internal/throttle/email.go lives in process memory; two API replicas each keep their own count.
ac-reset-throttle-fourth is ambiguous about whether the counter keys on the email as typed or case-folded; that mismatch lets a mixed-case address bypass it.
ac-reset-link-expires: the link expires after 30 minutes; also test a link opened at 29 minutes.
Document POST /password-resets and its 202 response in api/openapi.yaml.
Repeated reset requests for the same email must be throttled; the plan does not say whether the throttle also applies per IP address.
